summary: Twin 1898 wooden range towers on the Kennebec River at Arrowsic, aligned to mark the channel; automated in 1990 and cared for since 1998 by The Range Light Keepers.

lens.where: original optic, 1898 (USLHS); current optic a 250 mm unit (USLHS, Maine Lights Today)

structures.note: At Fiddler's Reach, about 1,075 feet up the reach from the dwelling (LighthouseFriends); the bell was removed in 1972 and a replacement mounted in 2016

access.note: Grounds open by land via a path from Doubling Point Road; dwelling and towers closed; visible from public cruises out of Bath and Boothbay Harbor.

facts.agency: The Range Light Keepers (nonprofit; owner since 1998 under the Maine Lights Program); US Coast Guard Aids to Navigation Team South Portland maintains the aid

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NRHP form and Maine Lights Today both give the front tower as 17 feet (5.2 m); LighthouseFriends' 21 feet is the outlier and is not used.
The NRHP form (four feet shorter than the front, about 13 feet) and Maine Lights Today (13 feet) agree; LighthouseFriends gives 18 feet.
The Bulletin of 1912 (PDF page 40) prints the commendation; LighthouseFriends dates the assistance to 1913. The story gives both dates and does not choose one.

notes_for_editor: 1) Separate station: the Doubling Point light (Board items 57-58; moved onto a stone foundation pier in fiscal 1900; Friends of the Doubling Point Light group) is a different light. Not written here; check for its own record. 2) Range (nautical miles): no source read gives one; the brief's range_nm 0.0 is unsupported and not carried forward. 3) Heights: the NRHP form, LighthouseFriends and Maine Lights Today differ for the front tower (17, 21, 17 feet); see resolved_conflicts. 4) Ransom B. Fuller grounding (1912) and the disabled-powerboat date (1912 Bulletin vs 1913 LighthouseFriends) are unresolved. The Bulletin commendation is dated 1912 only by the volume. 5) The 1912-1917 index (PDF page 34) lists Pierce's rescues at pages 40 and 240 without dates; the Bulletin page 240 was not read, and LighthouseFriends' 6 October 1916 rescue is not tied to it in the story. 6) Automation: brief lists 1988; USLHS and Maine Lights Today say 1990 (see corrections). Wikipedia's infobox (1988) is not cited. 7) Current ownership and access: LighthouseFriends says Coast Guard personnel still live in the dwelling; Maine Lights Today and LighthouseFriends both say the lights are owned by The Range Light Keepers. The story gives the owner and says the dwelling is closed; it does not state who lives there. 8) Chronicling America searches (Ransom B. Fuller, Doubling Point, Maine, 1912) returned no hits after loc.gov HTTP 520 errors; the first search for 1895-1915 failed outright. No newspaper source used. 9) Post-1960 keepers (McLean, Dan and Karen; Dail, Brown, etc.) are named only as the USLHS roster and the Friends' public role print them. LighthouseFriends' personal details about the McLeans are left out. 10) Karen McLean was a Coast Guard keeper; LighthouseFriends calls her in charge of the range lights, which the roster also does (1982-1987). 11) Facts for the 1990 automation and the Range Light Keepers' ownership rest on USLHS, Maine Lights Today and LighthouseFriends; no official Coast Guard record was read. 12) Fact-check pass 2026-10-22: the story now says downriver from Bath (LighthouseFriends' map caption: ships 'bound up the river to Bath' pass the lights; the NRHP form gives the city as Bath, vicinity; the Maine Lights Today coordinates, 43 deg 52.97 N, put the lights south of Bath). 13) Dates: the three Light-House Board volumes are labelled by fiscal year in the story (ended 30 June 1892, 1895, 1896, 1899 and 1900). 14) The 1928 Bulletin text gives the 12 August 1927 rescue; LighthouseFriends says only 'earlier that year'. The 1926 Bulletin (PDF page 18) lists the station's efficiency flag holder for 1925; the 1931 Bulletin (PDF page 10) names the station's keeper for the 1931 pennant. 15) The 1926 efficiency-flag list (PDF page 18) is an OCR table: the station is matched by name, and the keeper column (Harry L. Nye) was matched by column position; the page image should be checked before the keeper's name is used. The story names Nye from the 1924-1929 index, the 1928 and 1931 Bulletins and LighthouseFriends; the 1926 table's keeper column is not relied on.
